newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ROBSON WANTS TO END RELIANCE ON RONALDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON WANTS TO END RELIANCE ON RONALDO.

text.p: Barcelona boss Bobby Robson is unhappy that his team relies so heavily on their outstanding Brazilian striker Ronaldo.
"We can't always expect Ronaldo to sort out the games for us," said Robson after Wednesday's 1-1 home draw with Tenerife that handed the lead in the Spanish first division to arch rivals Real Madrid.
"He shouldn't be the key...he's 20 years old and has been up against some very experienced markers." added Robson.
Ronaldo was shut out by Tenerife defender Cesar Gomez and failed to score for the first time in four games.

With five league goals in six games the 2.5 billion peseta ($19.5 million) forward has shot to the top of the goalscoring tables and become unquestionably the biggest star in the country's star-studded league.
But other players in Spain's most expensive line-up have failed to come up with the goods, and Barcelona's good start has been in spite of some sloppy performances.
Robson's predecessor, former Dutch world cup star Johan Cruyff, criticised Robson's new-look Barcelona earlier in the week.
But club vice president Joan Gaspart has risen to Robson's defence.
"If Cruyff doesn't say bad things about Barcelona, he'll be a nobody," said Gaspart in an interview published in sports daily As on Thursday.
